verdict: FLAT, no stub, no resting orders (conv 3/10) — the court was convened around a binary that does not exist. Decisive = a DATE: Tessenderlo struck $13.30 on 6/30 against a FY guide reaffirmed 4/29; 29 days later (7/29) FMC cut FY26 to $620-680M EBITDA / $1.19-1.49 EPS and guided Q3 EBITDA -45%, EPS -90%. The 26% 'premium' is one guide cut the anchor never saw — red wins outright, blue verified every date. $13.30 also bought GOVERNANCE, not a clearing price (board seat + observer, standstill, top-up-to-20%, 8 demand registrations, 36-MONTH lock-up + post-lock-up transfer bans) — the anchor is contractually barred from defending the price it set. Blue reduced red twice, rightly: red compared ~$96M ANNUAL interest on the 8.000% secured notes to QUARTERLY EBITDA (true quarterly coverage ~5-6x), and the $1.2B upsized secured issue RETIRES the 3.200% Oct-2026 notes — the near-term wall is GONE; not STRUCTURAL, which is exactly why this is FLAT-on-no-edge rather than a short. Blue's own finding settles sizing and cuts against the bull: the takeover floor was not covenant-foreclosed (vote-with-board EXCLUDES change-of-control; standstill falls away on a CoC) — it was MARKET-TESTED AND ABSENT: the Tessenderlo minority raise was the disclosed CONCLUSION of the Board's Feb-2026 whole-company strategic review. At EV ~$5.13B ~7.9x FY26-mid EBITDA (~6.5x pro-forma) there is no distressed multiple, the Q3 guide still deteriorates, and no bid sits underneath. A fairly-priced deteriorating business — the one profile RP_FAIR does not cover.
